issues.description: Fast-path regex /\dm?s/i is an unstated second specification of 'contains a time token' that can drift from the parser.
issues.detail: The cheap pre-filter and the valueParser walk are now two implementations of the same predicate with no shared spec. The invariant — regex false means no time token — must stay in lockstep with the parser if CSS time units ever evolve. A short comment or named helper (hasTimeToken) tying the regex to the unit list would protect the abstraction.

issues.description: Regex /\dm?s/i over-approximates: it matches digit+s substrings inside URLs, strings, or identifiers.
issues.detail: Patterns like url(foo1s.png) or class-3s-foo will pass the gate. Correctness is preserved because the slow path still validates, so this is a deliberate over-approximation rather than a bug. A one-line comment marking it as an intentional over-approximation gate would make the looseness honest instead of hidden behind a confident name.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously approves this change as a textbook small, data-driven performance fix: a cheap regex short-circuits the expensive valueParser walk when no time-like token is present, and reordering the vendor.unprefixed call after the guard avoids needless work on skipped decls. Correctness is preserved because the slow path remains the source of truth. The only consensus concerns are minor and documentation-level: the regex is an unstated second specification of 'has time token' that must stay aligned with the parser, and it deliberately over-approximates by matching digit+s substrings in unrelated contexts. A brief comment naming both facts would harden the module without changing behavior.
